From Grok: 

The January 1943 Casablanca Conference was a wartime strategy meeting between Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill, not a full summit of all Allied leaders. 

It ran from 14 to 24 January at the Anfa Hotel outside Casablanca, in French Morocco, which the Allies had just taken in the North African campaign.

Joseph Stalin was invited and declined. The Red Army was in the middle of the Stalingrad offensive, and he did not want to leave the Soviet Union. Charles de Gaulle and Henri Giraud, rival leaders of the Free French, were brought in so the Americans and British could push them toward a working arrangement. 

The Combined Chiefs of Staff did most of the detailed military planning.
The main decisions were:

•  Germany first. The Allies would keep the main effort against Germany, while still holding and pressing Japan in the Pacific.

•  No cross-Channel invasion in 1943. Instead of an immediate landing in northern France, they chose the Mediterranean: finish North Africa, invade Sicily (later Operation Husky), and try to knock Italy out of the war. Forces would still be built up in Britain for a later invasion of France.

•  A heavier bomber offensive against Germany, and more shipping and supplies for the Soviet Union.

•  Priority on the Battle of the Atlantic, because U-boats were still threatening the supply line.

The meeting is best known for the unconditional-surrender announcement. At the final press conference on 24 January, Roosevelt said the Allies would accept nothing short of the unconditional surrender of Germany, Italy, and Japan. He compared it to Ulysses S. Grant’s Civil War nickname, “Unconditional Surrender”, Grant said it meant the destruction of those regimes’ war power and conquest ideology, not of their civilian populations. 

Churchill publicly backed it. 

Historians still argue about whether Roosevelt sprang it on the press; the U.S. record indicates he had settled on the policy before leaving Washington. 

Critics later claimed it stiffened German resistance by leaving no room for a negotiated exit; defenders said any terms the Allies would actually have offered were unacceptable to Hitler anyway.

The conference set the Allied pattern for 1943: Sicily and Italy, strategic bombing, aid to the USSR, and a delayed invasion of France, which was taken up again at later meetings such as Tehran and Quebec.

The title is not a slogan. He has been deposed for publishing a tape. A former board member who helped remove him from the shop he founded was recorded wishing the bullet had been his instead of Charlie Kirk’s and saying he fed the Southern District material to try to put him in prison. O’Keefe published it. The answer was a stalking petition, a temporary order, and police in the newsroom taking the guns. The order was later overturned. He is still being deposed for the story. That is the price on the door.

https://t.co/6Qqqcxu1H8

The method is the same one the networks retired: a hidden camera, a named person, the words on tape, then the confrontation. In January 2023, a man identified as Pfizer’s Jordon Trishton Walker, director of research and development strategic operations, said on camera that they were exploring mutating the virus themselves so vaccines could be built ahead of the strains. He called it directed evolution and said not to tell anyone. When O’Keefe played it back, Walker smashed the iPad.

https://t.co/XhPLLYqf6d

This year, the same method went back to Skid Row. A petition worker offered two dollars to sign someone else’s name, told the journalist to keep quiet because the police were close, and was the same man from the earlier cash-for-ballots tape. California Elections Code § 18603 makes paying for a petition signature a misdemeanor. The first round of that reporting was followed by a Justice Department investigation. The second round found the same corner still open.

https://t.co/8jPvmM6w9m

Real journalism is a primary source with a name and a date, published when the subject would rather it not be, and stood behind when the subject sues. The comedy interview is the night off. The work is the tape.

-April 13, the US Navy opens the blockade over marine radio: "The U.S. has announced a formal blockade of Iranian ports and coastal areas."

text:
I love all of my friends and collaborators who are laser-focused on building exceptional startup communities here in the Midwest.

BUT, I think most "flyover country vs SF/NYC" conversations and strategies are incorrectly zero sum. The framing is often "how can we be the next SF" or "how can ensure founders have no reason to leave."

I don't think this is a founder-centric POV - it's an ecosystem-centric POV. And while it's perfectly fine to aspire to offer a better experience to founders who live/work in your communities, it's not realistic in the near term to serve all of their capital, talent and customer needs.

SF/NYC will, on any reasonable time horizon worth considering today, be the center of the capital and AI talent markets. And that's great - such concentration is actually quite useful and efficient for founders everywhere.

Alternatively, there is great distribution across geographies on customer access (esp if you're not selling to other software/AI companies), specialized talent outside software engineering, and unique culture/quality of life considerations.

The reality is that these ecosystems need each other - SF/NYC founders largely need customers & specialized talent outside those hubs and non-coastal founders need access to the capital & talent density in SF/NYC. I'm regularly talking to coastal HQ'd founders who are eager for customer and talent connects in the Midwest, for example. And this is clearly true for Midwest companies, who are routinely faced with capital access constraints and regional investors who are looking for pricing arbitrage, not fair market deals.

The key is to build bridges that make it easier for founders, capital & talent to connect more efficiently from and to the coasts. When an ecosystem pushes a narrative they are creating an "all-in-one" startup community that presumes to give founder every resource, that's an economic development agenda, not a founder-friendly one. 

The non-coastal startup communities that will ultimately be the most sought-out by founders will be the ones who build the best bridges. The more we embrace the built-in advantages SF/NYC have, and those that we, the Midwest kings, have, the better outcomes we will create for founders EVERYWHERE.

text:
DRDO Goes Down Under: India Pavilion Opens at Land Forces 2026, Perth

WHAT
DRDO is taking part in Land Forces 2026, Australia's largest land defence exhibition, as part of the India Pavilion. Senior Australian officials visited the DRDO stall and opened talks on possible collaboration.

WHO
→ Ms. Kajari Biswas, Consul General of India for Western Australia and the Northern Territory, inaugurated the pavilion and spoke with DRDO officials about the technologies on show
→ David Nockels, First Assistant Secretary, and Simeon Ward, Chief Program Officer of ASCA, the Advanced Strategic Capabilities Accelerator, visited the stall and reviewed the systems

WHEN AND WHERE
October 6-8, 2026, in Perth. This is the first time the biennial show has been held in Perth. The 2024 edition drew nearly 1,000 exhibitors from 31 nations.

WHAT DRDO IS SHOWING
Reports list these as part of the display:
→ VL-SAM, a vertically launched air defence missile system developed for the Indian Navy
→ A heavy-weight torpedo
→ The Military Combat Parachute System (MCPS)
→ The Zorawar light tank, most likely as a scaled model

WHY ASCA MATTERS
ASCA is the Australian Defence organisation that fast-tracks new technology into service. Its officials stopping at the DRDO stall suggests Australia is looking at what Indian labs can offer, not just being polite.

WHAT WE DON'T KNOW
Which technologies the Australian delegates were most interested in, and whether the talks lead to anything formal. The reports only say they opened discussions "to explore potential avenues for future collaboration".

WHY IT MATTERS
India and Australia are already close partners in the Indo-Pacific. Showing homegrown torpedoes, missiles and parachutes in Perth moves the conversation from buying Western equipment to offering our own. Watch for any follow-up talks with ASCA.

text:
As the United States and China vie for A.I. dominance, the Trump administration has tightened hiring rules for foreign researchers, while Beijing has made recruiting global scientific talent a national priority.

Over the past two years, China has launched dedicated scientist visas and lucrative grants to attract international researchers, but foreign scientists are largely not coming.

Compounding the problem for Beijing, the number of Chinese scientists working in the United States has actually increased, according to a global A.I. research study by the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

The study found that for every 30 Chinese A.I. researchers working in the United States in 2025, only one researcher in China made the journey in reverse.

Damien Ma, who led the study, noted that despite bilateral tensions, the share of Chinese-origin researchers working in the United States rose by four percentage points compared with three years ago.

Analyzing paper authors from last year's NeurIPS conference, the researchers confirmed that the United States and China generate the bulk of frontier A.I. work, but through contrasting talent models.

While China excels at retaining homegrown talent educated domestically, the United States maintains its edge by drawing foreign specialists from China, India, South Korea, and elsewhere.

Because the data reflects long-term migration paths, experts suggest the high count of Chinese researchers in the United States may reflect decisions made before recent U.S. visa curbs and funding cuts took effect.

Syracuse University professor Yingyi Ma pointed to a lag effect, warning that any compounding erosion of America's appeal to top international talent will take years to fully register in the data.

China has nonetheless emerged as a powerful domestic research powerhouse, with 12 of the top 30 paper-publishing institutions at NeurIPS in 2025 based in China, up from six in 2022.

Peking University and Tsinghua University led the global rankings ahead of American institutions like M.I.T. and Stanford, while Chinese authors accounted for 41 percent of published authors compared with 34 percent from the United States.

Kevin Xu of Interconnected Capital noted that domestic firms like DeepSeek and Moonshot now offer comparable prestige to Silicon Valley leaders like OpenAI, giving local engineers little incentive to leave.

At the same time, authorities have increasingly limited outbound movement, recently blocking the founders of startup Manus from departing during an acquisition bid by Meta and expanding travel restrictions on other A.I. professionals.

China has found more success in convincing overseas Chinese talent to return, highlighted by Tencent's hiring of former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu as its chief A.I. scientist.

Yet for non-Chinese researchers, Silicon Valley continues to offer superior compensation and investment ecosystems, while China's language barriers, strict internet controls, and cultural insulation remain formidable hurdles.

to all the geothermal believers out there, the flippening has come 

in NV Energy’s 2026 filing, 3 geothermal offers came in at $105–107/MWh, below the ~$114/MWh capacity-weighted average for 11 solar + bess offers

in Nevada, of all the sunny places

the 3 solar + bess projects NV Energy put forward in 2024 averaged ~$94/MWh, but this 2026 slate is pricier, e.g., Boulder Solar III’s levelized price jumped from ~$85/MWh to ~$125/MWh after permitting delays, land carrying costs, higher financing costs, and, of course, big, bad tariffs.

could geothermal pull off a solar + wind circa 2010 move and scale faster to come down the cost curve? it now has a much longer tax-credit runway than new solar + wind projects (oh how the tables have turned), plus firm output and higher energy density (all true for nuclear too)

and for the 24/7 solar crowd: the ~$114/MWh average covers solar paired mostly with 4-hour batteries, and we all know 12+ hours of storage would cost more and still wouldn’t cover multi-day gaps

it might be time for more geothermal, people

Correct in part. As a RFA, any offer sheet the Fever didn’t/can’t match she can bounce as an RFA. Th y cannot core her until she hits the UFA.

When Caitlin Clark becomes a restricted free agent, the Indiana Fever will hold a powerful mechanism called the "Right of First Refusal." This means she can explore the open market, but the Fever ultimately control where she plays.

1. She Can Sign an "Offer Sheet" with Another Team
Clark would be permitted to negotiate with any of the other franchises in the league. If she finds a team she likes, she can sign a formal contract proposal with them called an offer sheet.

2. The Fever Have the Right to Match
Once Clark signs an offer sheet with a rival team, the Indiana Fever are given a specific window of time to look at the contract terms. The Fever then have two choices:
• Match the Offer: If Indiana chooses to match the exact financial and contract terms of the offer sheet, Clark must remain with the Fever. She does not have the option to decline or insist on leaving.
• Decline to Match: If the Fever choose not to match the offer, Clark is free to join the new team.

3. The "Sign-and-Trade" Alternative:

If Clark explicitly wants out and a rival team wants to sign her, the Fever don't have to let her walk for nothing. They can match the contract offer sheet and immediately work out a sign-and-trade deal. This allows Clark to get to her desired destination while ensuring Indiana receives high-value draft picks or star players in return.

Because Clark is an generational, franchise-altering talent who drives unprecedented ticket sales and viewership, the Fever will almost certainly match any outside offer sheet she receives. Structurally, restricted free agency makes it nearly impossible for a superstar to leave her original team against their will.

text:
月の満ち欠けと農作業・発酵を結びつける伝統、ドイツ語圏の資料（Demeter、biodynamische Landwirtschaft）を読み込んでいて、面白い構造に気づきました。

これらの体系には二つの層があります。①「満月前の種まきは避ける」「下弦の月は除草に良い」といった具体的な作業手順＝プロトコル層。②ノコギリソウやカモミールといった調合剤の名前や、なぜそれを使うのかという由来の物語＝ナラティブ層。そしてForschungsringが13年かけてプロトコル層を実際に反証実験で検証した、という記録も見つけました。つまりこの体系は、ただの言い伝えではなく「検証可能な手順」として扱われてきた、ということです。

これは、技術伝承を支える仕組みとして、ヲシテ文字や稲作技術にも応用できる補助線かもしれない、と私は考えています。字形そのもの（プロトコル）と、なぜその字形が生まれたかという文脈（ナラティブ）を分けて構造化する——これがまだ私の仮説の実装段階で、これからさらに掘り下げてみたいところです。

While reading German-language sources on biodynamic farming and its lunar calendar traditions, I noticed an interesting structure.

These systems have two layers: ① concrete work protocols (e.g. "avoid sowing before full moon," "weed during the waning moon in Capricorn"), and ② the narrative layer—the names and origin stories of preparations like yarrow or chamomile. I also found that the Forschungsring actually ran a 13-year falsification experiment on the protocol layer. This tells me the tradition wasn't just folklore—it was treated as a testable procedure.

I'm hypothesizing (still a work in progress) that this same two-layer approach—separating the "protocol" of how a character is written from the "narrative" of why that form emerged—could offer a useful scaffold for passing down Hoshite script and rice-farming techniques to the future.

2.5 TheEpistle of Enoch (Chapters 91-108) The Ethiopian Book of Enoch Canonical 

The fifth and final section of 1 Enoch is the most directly ethical and the most concerned with the immediate social conditions of its original audience. 

The Epistle of Enoch - chapters 91 through 108, with the embedded Apocalypse of Weeks (chapters 93 and 91:11-17) - is a sustained denunciation of the wealthy and powerful who oppress the righteous poor, combined with a promise of their eventual destruction and the vindication of those they have wronged 

The woes are searing. "Woe to you who build your houses through the toil of others, and every part of you is built by sin" 

(1 Enoch 99:13). "Woe to you who love the deeds of unrighteousness.

 Why do you hope for good for yourselves? 

Know that you shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous, and they shall cut off your necks and slay you and show you no mercy" (1 Enoch 98:12). 

This is the language of prophetic denunciation in the tradition of Amos and Isaiah, but stripped of any remaining patience. 

The righteous have suffered long enough. 

The judgment is imminent.

 The Apocalypse of Weeks, embedded near the beginning of the Epistle, offers the most compressed version of the Enochic theology of history. 

All of time is divided into ten weeks. 
Enoch himself lives in the seventh generation of the first week the primordial period of humanity's beginning.
 The Torah is given in the third week.
 The Temple is built in the fourth. The chosen people fall into wickedness in the fifth. 
In the sixth week, the whole generation of the godless forgets wisdom, and a man ascends (probably a reference to Elijah, the other translated figure of the Hebrew Bible). 

The seventh week is the present - a generation of apostasy in which the righteous minority receives the sevenfold teaching of all creation. 

The eighth week will see the great sword given to the righteous. 

The ninth will see the judgment of all works. 

In the tenth week, the angels of heaven will be judged, the old heaven will pass away, and a new heaven will appear.

It is a remarkable scheme - ten weeks of history, the present situated in the penultimate phase before the great transformation, the final iudgment close enough that the ethical urgency of the Epistle makes complete sense.

 The poor do not need to endure injustice forever. They need to endure it a little longer. The tenth week is coming.

text:
My fellow Americans,
I am speaking to you tonight about a habit that has grown comfortable in parts of this country and dangerous in its effects. It is the habit of endorsing systems, movements, and slogans from a safe distance, then treating the distance as proof of virtue. I am speaking in particular to Americans who say they support communism, who say they support socialism as a governing system rather than as a word for kindness, and who march under the banner of “Free Palestine” as if the banner itself settled the hardest questions. I am not speaking to every person who wants Palestinians to live in peace and dignity. I am speaking to the people who have turned a political program into a moral identity, and who have done it without ever living under the thing they praise.
Here is what I want to say to you.
Spend a year there. Not a week. Not a conference. Not a guided tour with a handler and a camera. A year. Live on the wages, under the laws, inside the institutions, and among the neighbors that your cause actually produces. Then come home, if you are allowed to come home, and tell us whether you still support what you support now. If you do, you will have earned the right to argue from experience. If you do not, you will have done the country a service by saying so out loud.
That is the whole idea. Everything else I am going to say is an explanation of why the idea is fair, why it is not a punishment, and why a free country is allowed to ask its own citizens to stop confusing sympathy with a system.
We are a free people. You may believe what you believe. You may organize, publish, protest, and vote. No president has the authority to outlaw an opinion, and I will not pretend otherwise. The First Amendment is not a favor I extend. It is a limit on me. So this is not a threat. It is a test. The test is simple because the claims are large. If a system is just, a year inside it should not break your loyalty to it. If a movement is liberation, a year among the people it claims to liberate should deepen your commitment, not complicate it. If the slogans survive contact with rent, bread, police, courts, schools, and the question of who is allowed to leave, then bring the slogans back and make the case. If they do not survive, stop asking the rest of us to applaud them.
Start with communism, because communism has the clearest record and the least excuse.
Communism is not a mood. It is a theory of ownership and power. It holds that private property in the means of production is the root of exploitation, that the state or the party must take that property, that markets in capital and land must be suppressed, and that a vanguard is entitled to rule until the new human being appears. That is not a cartoon. It is what the doctrine says, and it is what the doctrine did wherever it held a state.
The twentieth century ran the experiment at scale. The Soviet Union, Mao’s China, Cambodia under the Khmer Rouge, North Korea, and the lesser copies did not fail because the wrong people briefly held the levers. They failed in the same direction, again and again: shortages, secret police, camps, famines produced by policy, the destruction of independent institutions, and a party that could not be removed by the people it ruled. The death toll from famine, execution, and camp systems runs into the tens of millions. You do not have to accept every figure in every book to accept the shape of the thing. A system that must seal its borders to keep its own citizens from fleeing has already answered the question it claims to be asking.
I know the reply. You will say that was not real communism. You will say the next attempt will be different because the last attempt was corrupted by personality, by peasants, by imperialism, by insufficient commitment. That reply has been available for a hundred years. It has never produced a communist state that people were free to leave and still chose to stay in large numbers. North Korea is communist. Cuba spent decades communist in the classical sense and still polices speech and exit. The places that grew rich after flirting with state socialism did it by letting markets back in, not by purifying the doctrine.
So here is the invitation. Spend a year in a country that still governs on that model. Live on the official wage. Buy food in the official shops. Say in public what you say on a campus here about the party, the police, and the right to organize against the state. Apply for an exit visa at the end of the year without a foreign government pulling strings for you. Then come back and tell us whether the theory survived the year. If the government will not let you in, that is also information. A system that will not accept friendly witnesses is not confident in its own case.
Now socialism, which is the harder word, because Americans use it to mean three different things.
The first meaning is the welfare state inside a market economy: public pensions, public schools, public hospitals, paid for by taxes on private enterprise. The United States already does a great deal of this. So do countries that are richer and freer than the places usually offered as proof. Calling that “socialism” is a labeling trick. Those countries have private property, private firms, stock markets, and the right to fire a government. They are not evidence for the abolition of capital.
The second meaning is democratic socialism as a program to socialize major industries, set prices and wages by politics, and treat profit as a defect to be managed out of existence. That program has been tried in pieces. Britain’s postwar nationalizations, Venezuela’s twenty-first-century socialism, and repeated experiments in price control and expropriation did not produce the stable abundance their advocates promised. Venezuela had oil, universities, and a democratic start. It got hyperinflation, mass emigration, and the hollowing out of independent institutions. People did not leave because they were tricked by foreign propaganda. They left because the grocery store failed and the currency failed and the police became an arm of the party.
The third meaning is moral: a desire that no one be poor, that illness not bankrupt a family, that work be dignified. That desire is not the property of any faction. A president who confuses that desire with a license to seize the productive machinery of the country is not being compassionate. He is refusing to learn.
If you support socialism in the second sense, spend a year where that program is in force, not where a capitalist economy funds a safety net and then gets relabeled. Open a shop. Hire a worker. Watch what the ministry does to your prices. Try to move your savings. Read the newspaper that criticizes the minister, if one exists. At the end of the year, tell us whether the shortage was a sabotage story or a design story. Americans who want a larger safety net can argue for a larger safety net here, with numbers, tradeoffs, and elections. Americans who want the socialization of production should be willing to live under it before they ask this country to adopt it.
I turn now to the activists who organize under “Free Palestine,” and I am going to be more precise than the slogan.
There are Palestinians who want a state beside Israel, an end to occupation and blockade arrangements that make ordinary life hard, and a politics that is not run by armed factions. There are Israelis who want the same peace and who have buried neighbors to get it. Those people are not my target tonight. My target is the activism that treats Israel as a settler project with no right to exist, that excuses or celebrates the murder of civilians, that chants for a Palestine “from the river to the sea” while refusing to say what happens to the Jews on that land, and that describes Hamas and allied groups as resistance rather than as the authors of a program of killing and hostage-taking.
On October 7, 2023, armed men from Gaza entered Israel, murdered civilians in their homes and at a music festival, burned people, raped, and took hostages, including children and the elderly. That is not a contested impression. It is what happened. Any movement that cannot say that clearly, before it says anything else, has already failed the minimum test of political adulthood. Grief for Palestinian civilians, of whom there have been many in the war that followed, does not require you to launder the people who started that war with a massacre.
Gaza has been governed by Hamas since 2007. Hamas is not a social-services agency that happens to have a military wing. Its charter tradition and its practice reject Jewish sovereignty, divert concrete and money into tunnels and rockets, and punish dissent. The West Bank is divided between Israeli security control and a Palestinian Authority that postpones elections, pays stipends tied to attacks, and has not built the clean institutions a state requires. Arab states have not, in the main, offered Palestinians citizenship and a future. They have often offered camps and a permanent cause. That fact is inconvenient to the march, which is why the march rarely dwells on it.
So spend a year there. Not in a hotel in a third country. In Gaza, if Hamas or whatever authority follows it will have you, under its rules, without a press flak and without an embassy extraction on speed dial. In a West Bank city, under the Palestinian Authority, for long enough to see how courts work, how critics fare, what is taught in schools, and what happens to a person who says in public that Jews are a people with a right to a state. Live on local wages. Use local hospitals. Ask about the tunnels, the rockets, the hostages who are still held, and the Palestinians jailed for speaking against the factions. Then come back and answer the question in plain language: do you still support the cause as you support it now?
I expect some of you will say the year is impossible, because Israel controls the crossings, or because the territory is at war, or because you would not be safe. Those objections are part of the answer. A political program that cannot host its own Western advocates for a year is not the liberated future it advertises. A movement that is safe to shout in New York and unsafe to live in Ramallah or Gaza City has a problem that is not primarily American. If your actual wish is a negotiated two-state peace with mutual recognition, security guarantees, and an end to pay-for-slay and rejectionism, say that, and you are in a different conversation. If your wish is the elimination of Israel and you are unwilling to live in the society you propose to build on its ruins, then the wish is a costume.
I want to answer the charge that this challenge is a trick, or a way of saying dissenters should get out.
It is not. I am not offering you a ticket into exile. I am offering you a standard you already apply to everyone else. You tell soldiers to understand the wars they fight. You tell executives to meet their workers. You tell police to walk the neighborhoods they patrol. You tell Americans who praise this country’s founding to read the parts that were cruel as well as the parts that were free. Apply the same rule to yourself. Admiration from a distance is cheap. A year is not.
It is also not an insult to the poor. The poorest places on earth are not poor because Americans refused to feel enough. Many are poor because of misrule, corruption, closed markets, and ideologies that treat production as theft. The way out has a pattern: secure property, open trade, usable courts, and a government that can be replaced. That pattern is not Western vanity. It is the pattern that turned South Korea, Taiwan, Botswana, and the Baltic states into places people try to enter. The pattern you are praising is the pattern people try to exit.
Nor is this a claim that America is beyond criticism. We have failures in housing, schools, addiction, debt, and the capacity of our institutions. Those failures are argued in public, reported by a free press, and corrected, when they are corrected, by elections and law. The comparison that matters is not between America and a slogan. It is between America and the places the slogan points to. On speech, exit, food, and the chance to change your rulers, the comparison is not close.
Let me say what I will not do.
I will not open a file on every student who attends a march. I will not treat a political opinion as a crime. I will not bar people from federal employment solely for a belief, as distinct from an act of violence, a material lie on a security form, or membership in a group that engages in terrorism. I will not pretend that every critic of Israeli policy is an antisemite, or that every critic of capitalism is a camp guard in waiting. Judgment belongs on conduct and on the content of the program, not on a slogan scanner.
What I will do is refuse the moral blackmail that says compassion requires you to endorse the system. Wanting Palestinians to have a decent life does not require you to endorse Hamas. Wanting workers to have bargaining power does not require you to endorse the abolition of private firms. Wanting medicine and pensions does not require you to endorse state ownership of industry. Those are separate questions. Conflating them is how serious countries get talked into unserious disasters.
The policy that follows from this speech is therefore a residency, not a punishment. We will fund a voluntary program. Americans who advocate communism as a governing system, socialism as socialization of production, or a Free Palestine program that rejects Jewish self-determination may apply to live for twelve months in a relevant country or territory, on ordinary local terms, and to report what they find. We will not pay for activism. We will pay for room, board at a modest local standard, language support, and insurance, in exchange for a public report at the end. No report, no claim to have taken the challenge. Participants may come home whenever they wish. The countries that refuse to admit them will be named. The countries that admit them and then obstruct them will be named as well.
That program is an offer. The argument stands without it. If you will not go, you may still speak. You should expect the rest of us to notice that you would not go.
I have one more thing to say to the people who are not in the march, and who have been told that noticing any of this makes them cruel.
You are allowed to want your country to remain a place of private life, free speech, and borders that mean something. You are allowed to distinguish between a refugee and an ideology. You are allowed to say that Jewish students should not be chased across a quad, and that saying so is not a position on every acre of the West Bank. You are allowed to prefer a politics that asks what works over a politics that asks what sounds righteous at a distance. Patriotism in this country is not a claim that we are pure. It is a claim that the arrangement we inherited, improved, and can still improve is better than the arrangements that require permission to leave.
To the supporters of these causes, I return to the sentence I began with.
Spend a year there. Live the laws, the prices, the schools, the prisons, and the exit rules. Then come back and tell us, in your own words, whether you still support the causes you support now. If the answer is yes, make the argument as a witness. If the answer is no, say that too. Either way, you will have replaced a chant with a finding.
This country will remain free enough for you to refuse the year. It will also remain free enough for your neighbors to judge the refusal. That is not oppression. That is what a republic sounds like when it is tired of being lectured by people who will not live the lecture.
Good night, and may God bless the United States of America.

🤖💻 OpenAI Resets Codex Usage Limits for Users

OpenAI has once again given Codex users some welcome news as the company provides additional usage-limit resets for eligible users.

Codex has become one of OpenAI’s most popular tools for software development, allowing users to delegate coding tasks, work through repositories and build software with the help of AI.

However, usage limits have become an important part of the Codex experience, particularly for users working on large or compute-intensive projects.

OpenAI has previously issued global and promotional resets, while some eligible users have also received banked resets that can be saved and applied when needed.

A banked reset is essentially a one-time refresh of eligible Codex usage windows. Depending on the offer, it can refresh both the 5-hour and weekly usage windows.

OpenAI says eligibility can vary depending on factors such as the user's plan, account status, region and the specific promotion. Future resets are also not guaranteed.

The move comes as Codex continues to expand rapidly. OpenAI's developer community announced in August that Codex had passed 20 million active users, highlighting the growing demand for AI-powered coding tools.

For developers, additional resets can mean more room to experiment, build projects and test increasingly complex workflows without immediately running into usage limits.

At the same time, OpenAI continues to distinguish between automatic resets and banked resets. Automatic resets are applied directly to eligible usage limits, while banked resets remain available until the user applies them or they expire.

The bigger picture is clear:

AI coding is moving from simple code generation toward increasingly sophisticated software-development workflows.

And as millions of developers use tools like Codex, managing compute, speed and usage limits is becoming just as important as improving the models themselves. 🚀

💻 More Codex users.
⚡ More AI-powered development.
🔄 More focus on usage limits and resets.

The AI coding race is getting more competitive—and developers are watching every update closely. 👀

STORY | PM Modi offers prayers at Delhi temple to mark completion of 25 years as head of government

Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered prayers at the Shri Vinayaka Temple here on Wednesday to mark the completion of 25 years as head of government and renewed his pledge to serve the country with utmost dedication.

Modi has been continuously serving as head of government -- first as chief minister of Gujarat for three terms and subsequently as prime minister of India after winning three Lok Sabha elections -- since October 7, 2001.

"Performed puja and offered prayers at the Shri Vinayaka Temple in New Delhi today. Prayed to Lord Shri Ganesha for the happiness, prosperity, and good health of all my family members across the country," Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.

He said he prayed that everyone be blessed by the grace of 'Vignaharta' (Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles), and that the nation continue to progress on the path of growth.

Government sources said the prime minister renewed his pledge to serve the country with utmost dedication as he completed 25 years as head of government by offering prayers at the Shri Vinayaka Temple, Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi.

text:
DAILY SCRIPTURE — OCTOBER 7, 2026

DON’T DESPISE THE SMALL BEGINNING

Zechariah 4:10 (NLT)

“Do not despise these small beginnings, for the LORD rejoices to see the work begin…”

Sometimes we become discouraged because what God is doing doesn’t look big enough yet.

We prayed for change—but only see a tiny improvement.

We started rebuilding something—but we’re nowhere near finished.

We planted something—and there’s barely anything coming through the soil.

We took one step toward God, but we’re looking at somebody who’s already twenty miles down the road.

And we think:

“Is this really accomplishing anything?”

Zechariah speaks into exactly that kind of discouragement.

God’s people were rebuilding the temple. Compared with what had existed before, the beginning didn’t look very impressive.

But God said:

Don’t despise the small beginning.

Imagine planting an acorn.

You place something tiny into the ground, cover it with dirt, and for a while it looks like absolutely nothing is happening.

But hidden beneath the surface, life has begun.

Years later, something you once could hold between two fingers can become an oak tree strong enough to withstand storms.

Never judge what God is growing only by what you can see today.

Maybe your “small beginning” is praying again.

Reading one chapter of Scripture.

Apologizing to your spouse.

Forgiving somebody.

Breaking one unhealthy habit.

Going back to church.

Making one phone call.

Starting something God has been putting on your heart.

Or simply getting back up after falling.

Don’t say:

“It’s only one step.”

One step with Jesus is still movement in the right direction.

We often celebrate the finished testimony while forgetting that nearly every testimony once looked unimpressive.

David once had a sling.

Moses had a staff.

A boy offered five loaves and two fish.

The disciples started as a small group following Jesus.

God has never been intimidated by small beginnings.

Sometimes we’re waiting for God to give us something enormous while He’s asking:

“What are you doing with the little thing I’ve already placed in your hand?”

Don’t compare your beginning with somebody else’s harvest.

Don’t quit because progress feels slow.

And don’t underestimate what Jesus Christ can do with something completely surrendered to Him.

Start small.
Stay faithful.
Keep going.
Let God determine how large it becomes.

TODAY’S MISSION

Choose one small thing you’ve been putting off because it doesn’t seem significant enough.

Do it today.

One prayer.
One apology.
One act of obedience.
One phone call.
One step.

Then thank God for allowing you to begin.

PRAYER

Father, forgive me for overlooking small beginnings. Help me stop measuring Your work by immediate results. Give me faithfulness in the little things and patience while You work beneath the surface. Take what I place in Your hands and use it according to Your purpose. Keep me from comparison and discouragement, and help me faithfully take today’s step with Jesus Christ. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

#FaithFamilyFreedom #DailyScripture #Zechariah410 #NLT #SmallBeginnings #StayFaithful #JesusChrist

text:
🇵🇰|What's happening in Pakistan isn't just a domestic political crisis or a simple protest. It's the visible eruption of a deeper conflict: a popular movement for sovereignty and justice colliding with a state apparatus that acts as a comprador for imperial interests.

Here is the architecture of that conflict.

📍 The Long March and the Demand for Khan

On October 4, 2026, a convoy of over 5,000 supporters of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) set out from Lakki Marwat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, led by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, on a 270km march to Islamabad. Their central demand is the release of Imran Khan, imprisoned since August 2023 and facing over 100 cases he says are politically motivated. His family and party say his health is deteriorating in jail, with lawyers stating he has lost significant vision in his right eye. The march was postponed once for talks, but those talks collapsed over the government's refusal to allow PTI leaders to meet Khan or arrange an independent medical exam.

🛑 The State's Response: Barricades and the "Law"

The government's response has been to militarize the capital. Authorities have stacked shipping containers to block key access routes, deployed thousands of police and paramilitary forces, and declared the marchers will not be allowed to enter Islamabad. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif offered talks on October 6, but warned that "the law will take its course" and accused PTI of harming the economy. This follows a pattern: a previous PTI protest in 2024 ended in violence, and police interventions to break up peaceful protests have doubled in 2026 compared to the previous year.

🔥 The Second Front: Rejecting the War for Saudi Arabia

This is the layer the mainstream narrative ignores. The protest is not only about Khan. Marchers are explicitly demanding that Pakistan stay out of the war against Iran and Yemen. This is not abstract. On October 5, under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye announced moves to "rapidly deploy military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia" to counter the Houthi offensive near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, is the architect of this pivot.

💰 The Comprador Logic: Why the Generals Serve

The question is why Pakistan's military leadership would drag the country into a war that threatens its own borders. The answer is profit and dependency. The Pakistan Army runs a vast economic empire (Fauji Foundation, Army Welfare Trust) worth billions. Saudi Arabia is a key patron. The Mecca Pact gives the generals a new revenue stream: deploying troops and selling military services to Riyadh. This is the comprador model: the military elite enriches itself by serving an external patron, while the costs inflation, instability, and war are borne by the public.

🕊️ The Real Stakes: Sovereignty vs. Servitude

The Long March and the anti-war movement are two expressions of the same demand: sovereignty. One demands the release of a popular leader who represents an independent political path. The other demands that Pakistan not be used as a proxy in a war that serves foreign interests. The state's response barricades, arrests, and a commitment to send troops to Yemen reveals whose interests it serves. The movement is not a "problem" for the government; it is a mirror reflecting the gap between the people and a state that acts as a franchise for empire.

text:
How do I believe we fix South Africa?
It starts at the top.

If the ANC were a person with a credit score, I’m pretty sure the person would be sitting somewhere around 300–400.

South Africa needs a new President — someone who is not ANC-affiliated. In my view, after more than 30 years in government, the ANC should no longer be entrusted with the Presidency.

But changing the President is only the beginning.

I believe there needs to be a comprehensive, independent investigation into serious allegations involving corruption, state capture, political violence and any credible allegations concerning the financing, support or instigation of terrorism.

Investigate it properly.

Follow the evidence.

Give everyone due process.

And if individuals are found guilty in a court of law, political status should offer absolutely no protection.

Nobody should be above the law.

Then we rebuild the institutions.

MINISTER OF POLICE

I believe the Minister of Police should be appointed based on merit and should operate without party-political interference.

Someone with the crime-focused approach of Ian Cameron represents the type of leadership I would like to see in that position.

Because the Minister of Police should have one job, one responsibility and one priority:

The safety of South African citizens and the pursuit of criminals within our borders.

That’s it.

No politics.

No cadre deployment.

No protecting politically connected individuals.

From the Minister downward, appointments within SAPS should be based on merit, competence, integrity and performance.

SAPS should become an institution that law-abiding South Africans trust — and criminals genuinely fear.

MINISTER OF JUSTICE

Then comes justice.

Because having effective police means nothing if criminals simply disappear into a dysfunctional justice system.

Our justice system needs teeth the size of a Megalodon.

Investigate.

Gather the evidence.

Give the accused a fair, evidence-based trial.

And if the evidence proves guilt beyond reasonable doubt:

Prosecute. Sentence. Enforce.

Efficiently. Effectively. Fairly.

No Mickey Mouse justice system where political influence, money or status determines how seriously the law applies to you.

Whether you are an unemployed citizen, a billionaire, a police officer, a Minister or the leader of one of South Africa’s largest political parties:

The law must apply equally.

And that includes politicians such as Julius Malema. Political power should never provide insulation from the consequences of a criminal conviction.

THEN FOLLOW THE MONEY.

Where someone is lawfully convicted of corruption, fraud or another crime involving proceeds of crime, use the asset-forfeiture mechanisms available under South African law.

Identify unlawfully acquired assets.

Freeze them where legally justified.

Seize them following due process.

Appoint competent, merit-based professionals to administer and liquidate those assets.

And where the money was stolen from the state:

Recover it for the state.

Crime should never be profitable.

MINISTER OF FINANCE

The same philosophy should apply to our finances.

Competence.

Merit.

Accountability.

South Africa needs financial leadership focused on fiscal sustainability, economic growth and protecting taxpayers — rather than serving party-political interests.

Because every billion rand wasted, stolen or irresponsibly borrowed today eventually becomes somebody else’s debt tomorrow.

And that “somebody else” is increasingly our children.

My entire argument can ultimately be reduced to a few principles:

MERIT OVER POLITICAL LOYALTY.

COMPETENCE OVER CADRE DEPLOYMENT.

JUSTICE WITHOUT POLITICAL PROTECTION.

POLICE WHO PROTECT CITIZENS.

A GOVERNMENT THAT RESPECTS TAXPAYERS.

AND ABSOLUTELY NOBODY ABOVE THE LAW.

Do that consistently for long enough — rebuild the institutions, restore accountability, reward competence and aggressively tackle corruption — and I genuinely believe South Africa could transform itself dramatically within 10–20 years.

We have the resources.

We have the infrastructure.

We have extraordinary people.

We have entrepreneurs, engineers, farmers, doctors, tradespeople, scientists, teachers, innovators and ordinary South Africans capable of building an incredible country.

What South Africa desperately needs is a state capable of turning that potential into results.

Not a liberation movement with a deeply controversial historical relationship with terrorism designations.

Not another 30 years of a currency losing enormous value.

Not politicians chanting inflammatory songs about killing people.

Not hollowed-out institutions.

Not corruption.

Not cadre deployment.

Not excuses.

We could go on…

But eventually, South Africa has to draw a line in the sand.

WE NEED MERIT!

WE NEED JUSTICE!

And the incredible thing about democracy?

Changing the direction of a country ultimately starts with something extraordinarily simple:

Drawing an X on a ballot paper.

That’s it.

Your vote.

Your decision.

Your voice.

4 NOVEMBER 2026.

LOCAL ELECTIONS.

EVERY. VOTE. COUNTS.

Every single one.

South Africa belongs to its people.

Use your democratic voice.

text:
Crypto Policy Group Sees Regulatory Momentum Despite Senate’s Clarity Act Defeat

Kristin Smith, president of the Solana Policy Institute and interim chief executive of the Blockchain Association, says the crypto industry is making regulatory progress in Washington despite the Senate’s failure to advance the Clarity Act. The proposed legislation would have established a federal framework for digital-asset markets, but Smith argues that agency-level action could still create lasting policy changes. She points to the stablecoin legislation known as the Genius Act and revisions to an IRS broker rule as examples of recent industry gains. The CFTC has also begun seeking public input on rules for leveraged retail crypto trading, while the SEC and CFTC are pursuing additional digital-asset rulemaking. Smith estimates these processes could take 18 to 24 months. She believes rules completed before roughly summer 2028 may become difficult for Congress to overturn under the Congressional Review Act, particularly if financial institutions and international companies begin building businesses around them. Smith considers renewed passage of a broader market-structure bill before or shortly after the 2026 midterm elections unlikely, citing unresolved concerns involving the president’s family crypto interests and limited support from banks. Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan offered a more cautious view, noting that agency rules could be reversed after a change in administration in 2029.

text:
The tremors are just noise,
but her resolve is a deep, quiet signal.
Muscles may rebel against the mind,
but they cannot shake the bedrock of her convictions
or slow the steady march of her spirit.

They look at the stiffness, the uneven stride,
and offer the heavy cloak of low expectations.
But she leaves their pity on the shelf,
choosing the hard, beautiful road of self-reliance,
standing tall on a foundation of faith and freedom.

Every step is a calculated victory,
every word an unyielding stance,
proving that liberty is not measured by perfect mechanics,
but by the fierce, unbroken will
to command your own destiny.

You are an inspiring person.

WWE Unreal Season 3 Is Coming: Cast, Release Date, Episodes, and What to Know

Go behind the scenes as John Cena says goodbye.

By Christopher Hudspeth

June 23, 2026

WWE Unreal is making its return with a fresh batch of behind-the-scenes action in Season 3.

After taking fans deeper than ever inside World Wrestling Entertainment’s creative process, the hit docuseries will once again pull back the curtain on some of the biggest moments, boldest decisions, and unforgettable storytelling with some of the WWE’s greatest legends who’ve shaped the industry and new stars who are emerging as prominent parts of the future.

What will be shown in WWE Unreal Season 3?

In WWE Unreal Season 3, John Cena says goodbye, a fan favorite returns, and the next generation of Superstars rise to the occasion.

The series takes viewers inside the writers room as injuries, last-minute pivots, and career-defining decisions reshape WWE’s biggest season yet heading into WrestleMania 42.

Who will be featured in WWE Unreal Season 3?

The cast of WWE Superstars featured in WWE Unreal Season 3 includes John Cena, Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, AJ Lee, Trick Williams, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer, Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Chelsea Green, Matt Cardona, Seth Rollins, and Becky Lynch.

When does WWE Unreal Season 3 come out?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will be released on July 21.

How many episodes are in WWE Unreal Season 3?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will have five 50-minute episodes.

Strap in and prepare to be a fly on the wall backstage during some of the WWE’s most riveting moments. (Netflix)

Netflix News

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

Bridgerton Season 4 — The Regency-era drama returns later in the month (Part 1 premiering around Jan 29), with plenty of masquerade glamour and romance — the premiere events are already making waves!

Other notables include:

Kidnapped: Elizabeth Smart (true-crime docuseries)

text:
Maureen Wanjiru Ngure, a 38-year-old Kenyan-born registered nurse who lived in California for 20 years, was deported to Kenya on September 22, 2026, following her detention by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Ngure arrived in the United States in 2006 on a visitor's visa and subsequently overstayed. She built a life in Concord, California, working as a registered nurse, contributing to Contra Costa County's COVID-19 frontline response, marrying a U.S. citizen, and raising two children.

Although she had an approved family petition through her marriage and no criminal record, a final removal order issued by an immigration judge in February 2012 remained unresolved.

On August 14, 2026, Ngure was detained during a routine, mandatory ICE check-in at the federal immigration headquarters in San Francisco. She was transferred across several holding facilities, ultimately being held in a Louisiana detention center.

At the time of her arrest, Ngure and her husband, Peter Mang'ara Muchendu, were actively preparing to relocate their family to Canada, where she had been offered a nursing position in British Columbia. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) maintained that pending foreign job applications or petitions do not confer legal status against an outstanding U.S. deportation order.

Following her deportation in late September, her husband and two children left the United States to reunite with her in Kenya.

text:
An independent autopsy is a post-mortem examination performed by a private, board-certified forensic pathologist outside of the government or medical examiner system. Families typically commission these private exams when they seek an impartial, secondary review to ensure transparency or to prepare for legal action. [1]
The term is currently central to the case of Nolan Wells, an 18-year-old Black college football player found dead in Mississippi in July 2026. [1]

The Purpose and Role of an Independent Autopsy
•Unbiased Analysis: It provides an objective look at the evidence, free from the systemic constraints or potential conflicts of interest within local law enforcement or municipal medical systems. [1]
•Discrepancy Identification: Private pathologists look for findings that may have been missed, omitted, or interpreted differently during the initial state-run autopsy. [1, 2]
•Legal Defensibility: The documented findings offer critical forensic evidence that civil rights attorneys and families can use in court or to push for deeper federal investigations. [1, 2]

Current Context: The Nolan Wells Case
In the ongoing investigation into Nolan Wells' death, the family’s independent autopsy has heavily shaped the legal narrative: [1, 2]

Feature
State Autopsy Findings
Independent Autopsy Findings (Dr. Roger Mitchell)
Cause of Death
Officially unreleased, though authorities suspect drowning.
Undetermined due to severe decomposition and missing evidence.
Head Trauma
Unspecified by state officials, but noted bruises on the back of the head.
Identified a massive 12x8 inch area of red discoloration (blunt-force trauma) on the back of the skull.
Limitations
Performed first; retained several primary internal organs.
Arrived with the anterior neck structures removed (trachea, hyoid bone), making it impossible to rule out strangulation or a neck injury.
Following a Mississippi grand jury's recent decision declining to bring criminal charges, prominent civil rights attorney Ben Crump and the Wells family have heavily cited these independent autopsy findings to formally demand a federal review of the case. [1]

text:
清 玉乳丁紋簋形爐

【玉乳丁紋簋形爐】
這件清代玉器名為「玉乳丁紋簋形爐」，現藏於國立故宮博物院。此器全高12.9公分，口徑9.7公分，底徑4.8公分，材質為青玉，呈灰青色，局部帶有赭色斑點。器形仿青銅簋器，整體構造包括撇口、束頸、圓鼓腹及圈足，工藝細膩。

器身兩側的耳朵刻為立體獸首，頸部裝飾有棱脊及簡化獸紋，口沿中央鑄有高凸小獸首，腹部下方則飾乳丁紋，表面肌理豐富且質感優雅。該爐配有木蓋，木蓋頂部置有白玉玉頂，玉色泛黃並附有大片赭斑，玉頂上以多層次鏤雕技法表現鴛鴦戲水圖案，鴛鴦口含荷葉，並有花莖穿插，細節生動傳神。木蓋蓋面飾有如意雲紋，增添華美之感。

清代玉器在形制和紋飾上多仿青銅器，反映清廷對傳統文化的承襲與創新。本件簋形爐不僅體現了青玉質地的典雅，還兼具雕刻技藝和紋飾藝術。造型上的獸首耳、角脊與乳丁紋均有青銅器風格，但玉質的光澤和細膩使器物呈現出獨特的柔潤美感。

觀賞此器時，應特別注意乳丁紋的配置與細節，該紋理在腹部低處環繞，呈現出乳釘排列的規律感，且與獸首造型呼應。口沿中央小獸首突出，顯示工匠對細節的講究。木蓋上鴛鴦鏤雕展示了多層次雕刻技巧，是器物融合材料及工藝的典範。

總之，玉乳丁紋簋形爐是清代玉雕的精美代表，結合了傳統青銅器形與玉雕特有的質感和細膩工藝。它不僅是藝術品，也是文化的載體，給予觀者同時感受歷史與匠心的視覺享受。

Jade Gui-Shaped Incense Burner with Knob Pattern

This exquisite Qing dynasty jade object, known as the "Jade gui-shaped incense burner with knob pattern," is housed in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. The piece measures 12.9 cm in total height, with a mouth diameter of 9.7 cm and a base diameter of 4.8 cm. Crafted from a grayish-green jade featuring localized ochre spots, the vessel faithfully imitates the form of a bronze gui, an ancient Chinese ritual vessel.

Its form comprises a flaring mouth rim, a constricted neck, a rounded belly, and a ring foot — classic features of the gui shape. The ears of the vessel are sculpted into upright animal heads, adding a dynamic, three-dimensional detail. The neck is adorned with ridges and simplified beast motifs, while the center of the mouth rim features a prominent small animal head raised in relief. On the lower belly, a pattern of knob-like protrusions known as the "knob pattern" or "ruled studs" provides a tactile surface decoration.

The vessel is topped with a wooden lid crowned by a white jade finial. The finial exhibits a yellowish tone and areas of broad ochre staining, carved with a multilayered openwork design depicting mandarin ducks holding lotus leaves in their beaks, interlaced by floral stems. The lid itself is decorated with auspicious ruyi cloud patterns, elegantly complementing the overall aesthetic.

Objects of this type and period commonly replicate bronze forms, reflecting the Qing court’s reverence for ancient ritual bronzes while adapting them in precious materials and refined workmanship. The combination of the jade's soft luster and the detailed carving results in a harmonious blend of traditional motifs and tactile refinement.

Viewers should focus on several key details: the knob pattern circling the lower abdomen offers a rhythmic, punctuated texture that contrasts with the smooth jade surface; the raised animal head on the mouth rim demonstrates the carver’s attention to precise, lively detail; and the multilayered carving of the lid’s finial, showing the mandarin ducks amidst botanical elements, exemplifies advanced jade carving techniques. Together, these elements showcase the artistic and technical sophistication of Qing jade craftsmanship.

In sum, this jade gui-shaped incense burner presents a layered dialogue between ancient bronze form and Qing-period jade artistry. It stands not only as an artwork but also as a cultural symbol, inviting appreciation for both its historical resonance and the meticulous skill behind its creation.

text:
Hey Steph, I ignore the $5, $10 or $100 price predictions and price suppression theories. 

I start with one question which what is XRP actually needed for?

The world is developing different forms of digital money: USD stablecoins, tokenised bank deposits, CBDCs, the digital euro, e-CNY and others. But privacy and data sovereignty deserve far more attention.

Different jurisdictions have different privacy, financial-data, AML/KYC and sanctions regimes. Governments want control over their monetary systems and sensitive transaction data. Citizens want privacy.

That makes dependence on a single foreign-controlled monetary system politically difficult. How do separately governed systems exchange value while retaining control over their domestic data?

And don’t confuse XRPL adoption with demand for XRP as a liquidity asset. This is where many influencers blur an essential distinction. An institution issuing stablecoins or tokenised assets on the XRP Ledger does not automatically mean it uses XRP to bridge those assets.

XRP is required for transaction fees and reserves, but those requirements alone do not establish the investment case for substantial cross-border liquidity demand.

The question that matters is how these systems obtain cross-border FX liquidity while reducing the need to pre-fund large foreign-currency balances—and whether XRP offers the most effective solution.

A bridge asset does not, by itself, guarantee privacy. That depends on the architecture, access controls and information exchanged.

If XRP wins a substantial role, the interesting numbers will be actual payment volumes, liquidity requirements and the XRP available to meet them.

If the financial system solves that problem more efficiently without XRP, the thesis changes.

My longer-term view is that the world would benefit from a neutral digital reserve asset. But that is a separate thesis, but I watch the IMF for any evidence.

These are the developments I watch for XRP’s wealth creation, the architecture, the adoption and the liquidity demand. Not influencers. Not price predictions.

The severe allegations stem from an altercation on October 29, 2023, during a Halloween party inside a hotel suite at Resorts World Las Vegas. According to witness accounts and text messages sent by Rodimer's own wife, the former athlete knocked Tapp to the ground, causing him to hit a table, and repeatedly punched and choked him. Following a months-long investigation, the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department issued an arrest warrant for Rodimer. He voluntarily surrendered to authorities on March 6, 2024, and was released after posting a $200,000 bond. Known politically for his unsuccessful campaigns as a GOP candidate for Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District in 2020 and Texas’s 6th Congressional District in 2021, Rodimer has pleaded not guilty to the open murder charge. Defense attempts to suppress text messages and wiretap evidence or dismiss the grand jury indictment were denied by a Clark County judge in July 2026, keeping the high-profile criminal case moving forward toward a trial.

Long before his 2024 murder charge, Rodimer accumulated an extensive record of violent allegations and police intervention that repeatedly hindered his political aspirations. His documented history of physical aggression dates back to 2010, when he was arrested for misdemeanor battery following an altercation at a Waffle House in Florida. Police records revealed he was harassing a group of women and assaulted a man who intervened, though Rodimer avoided a conviction by completing a court-ordered anger management program.
